title: Managed local model serving
description: User-approved managed Ollama CPU service, curated IFM K2 Horizon 3.7B/7B and Qwen3.8 27B Q4_K_M artifacts, persistent installation controls and content-grounded local generation. No automatic weight download/load or paid fallback.
acceptance_criteria: Given no hosted key or local weights, when Compose starts, then the core app is ready and all local catalog choices remain visible but unavailable.
Given a model transfer, when the browser closes or services restart, then durable job/progress state survives; manual pause stays paused until explicit resume.
Given verified local weights, when summaries or Q&A run, then the native provider preserves document citations, context limits, histories and request UUID safety without hosted charges.
Given a saved local default, when weights are deleted, then default/history survive and generation is blocked until reinstall or explicit selection change.
Given the exact 7B artifact, when the reviewed engine runs on the authorized host, then real streaming, structured output, hashes, reasoning and resource behavior are measured.
test_cases: ARA-044 runtime protocol/race/server and opt-in 7B checks.
ARA-045/046 isolated real-service SQL/API and provider/context regression tests.
ARA-047 RTL and ARA-048 fixture browser journeys for durable controls/default/history.
verification: Implemented and independently reviewed on feat/managed-ollama; main unchanged, no GitHub push. Lead final backend 185 passed in 38.77 seconds with Ruff/build/migration/bucket init; frontend 356 across 54 files plus strict TypeScript/ESLint/build; fresh full Playwright 12 passed in 2.0 minutes, then two deletion/local-generation tests passed after the sampling correction. Real ARM64 CPU 7B app summary/Q&A with no OpenAI key and zero hosted reservations, exact provenance snapshot, retained original PDF/history/default/weights after six-service restart. Default startup: 20.91 MiB Ollama, no installed/loaded weights. Only 7B/ARM64 CPU tested; other catalog models/hardware require their own validation.
